source.grammarPolicy: All 36 patterns from the appended index, four per unit; two original app questions per pattern, not textbook exercises. Present, future and past inference and the prediction use of -(으)ㄹ까요 remain distinct.

source.normalization: Same-meaning duplicates merge only within unit/difficulty, preserving source occurrences and literal glosses. Split slash pairs retain combined sourceHeadword/sourceGloss. Awkward English is clarified for study while original glosses remain literal.

grammar.meaning: be called; report a name or label

questions.prompt: Introduce your name using N(이)라고 해요: 저는 민수___ 해요.
questions.explanation: Use 라고 after a vowel-ending noun and 이라고 after a consonant-ending noun to report a name or label.

questions.prompt: Report the label using N(이)라고 해요: 이것은 한복___ 해요.
questions.explanation: Use 라고 after a vowel-ending noun and 이라고 after a consonant-ending noun to report a name or label.

grammar.meaning: in order to; intended purpose

questions.prompt: Use -(으)려고 with 읽다: 책을 ___ 도서관에 왔어요.
questions.explanation: Use -으려고 after most consonants and -려고 after a vowel to state the purpose of an action.

questions.prompt: Use -(으)려고 with 배우다: 한국어를 ___ 한국에 왔어요.
questions.explanation: Use -으려고 after most consonants and -려고 after a vowel to state the purpose of an action.

grammar.meaning: introduce a noun as background

questions.prompt: Use N인데: 제 고향은 부산___ 바다가 아름다워요.
questions.explanation: 인데 attaches to a noun to introduce background for the following information. It is used after both vowel and consonant endings.

questions.prompt: Use N인데: 저는 학생___ 한국어를 공부해요.
questions.explanation: 인데 attaches to a noun to introduce background for the following information. It is used after both vowel and consonant endings.

grammar.meaning: long negation

questions.prompt: Negate 비싸다 using -지 않아요: 이 식당은 ___ .
questions.explanation: Attach -지 않다 directly to the verb or adjective stem: 비싸지 않아요, 먹지 않아요.

questions.prompt: Negate 먹다 using -지 않아요: 저는 고기를 ___ .
questions.explanation: Attach -지 않다 directly to the verb or adjective stem: 비싸지 않아요, 먹지 않아요.

grammar.meaning: turn an action into a noun phrase

questions.prompt: Use 읽다 and -는 것: 저는 책을 ___ 좋아해요.
questions.explanation: Verb stem + 는 것 turns an action into a noun phrase. Add 을 when that phrase is an object: 읽는 것을, 요리하는 것을.

questions.prompt: Use 요리하다 and -는 것을: 저는 주말에 ___ 좋아해요.
questions.explanation: Verb stem + 는 것 turns an action into a noun phrase. Add 을 when that phrase is an object: 읽는 것을, 요리하는 것을.

grammar.meaning: know or not know how to do something

questions.prompt: Express knowing how with 만들다: 저는 김밥을 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다 expresses knowing/not knowing how. ㄹ-final 만들다 becomes 만들 줄; 읽다 becomes 읽을 줄.

questions.prompt: Express not knowing how with 읽다 and -(으)ㄹ 줄 몰라요: 저는 한자를 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다 expresses knowing/not knowing how. ㄹ-final 만들다 becomes 만들 줄; 읽다 becomes 읽을 줄.

grammar.meaning: or between nouns

questions.prompt: Connect nouns with or: 토요일___ 일요일에 만나요.
questions.explanation: Use 이나 after a consonant-ending noun and 나 after a vowel-ending noun to offer alternatives.

questions.prompt: Connect nouns with or: 커피___ 차를 마셔요.
questions.explanation: Use 이나 after a consonant-ending noun and 나 after a vowel-ending noun to offer alternatives.

grammar.meaning: or between actions

questions.prompt: Use -거나 with 보다: 쉬는 날에는 영화를 ___ 음악을 들어요.
questions.explanation: Attach -거나 directly to the verb stem to connect alternative actions.

questions.prompt: Use -거나 with 읽다: 주말에는 책을 ___ 산책을 해요.
questions.explanation: Attach -거나 directly to the verb stem to connect alternative actions.

grammar.meaning: try an action; have experience doing it

questions.prompt: Use 먹다 with -아/어 봤어요: 저는 김치를 ___ .
questions.explanation: The past form -아/어 봤어요 describes having tried or experienced an action: 먹어 봤어요, 가 봤어요.

questions.prompt: Use 가다 with -아/어 봤어요: 저는 제주도에 ___ .
questions.explanation: The past form -아/어 봤어요 describes having tried or experienced an action: 먹어 봤어요, 가 봤어요.

grammar.meaning: because; reason for a suggestion or instruction

questions.prompt: Use 춥다 with -(으)니까: 밖이 ___ 따뜻한 옷을 입으세요.
questions.explanation: -(으)니까 or N(이)니까 gives a reason and can precede advice or an instruction. 춥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 추우니까. 휴일 takes 이니까.

questions.prompt: Use N(이)니까: 오늘은 휴일___ 푹 쉬세요.
questions.explanation: -(으)니까 or N(이)니까 gives a reason and can precede advice or an instruction. 춥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 추우니까. 휴일 takes 이니까.

grammar.meaning: for a period of time

questions.prompt: Say for three days: 사흘 ___ 여행했어요.
questions.explanation: Place 동안 after a duration noun phrase to state how long an action lasts.

questions.prompt: Say for two hours: 두 시간 ___ 공부했어요.
questions.explanation: Place 동안 after a duration noun phrase to state how long an action lasts.

grammar.meaning: after completing an action

questions.prompt: Use -고 나서 with 먹다: 아침을 ___ 약을 먹었어요.
questions.explanation: Attach -고 나서 to a verb stem to show that the next action occurs after the first is completed.

questions.prompt: Use -고 나서 with 끝내다: 숙제를 ___ 게임을 했어요.
questions.explanation: Attach -고 나서 to a verb stem to show that the next action occurs after the first is completed.

grammar.pattern: V-는 것 같다, A-(으)ㄴ 것 같다, N인 것 같다
grammar.meaning: seem; infer a present action or state

questions.prompt: Infer a current action using 자다: 방이 조용해요. 아이가 ___ . (Use -는 것 같아요.)
questions.explanation: For present inference, action verbs take -는 것 같다, adjectives take -(으)ㄴ 것 같다, and nouns take 인 것 같다.

questions.prompt: Infer a present quality using 작다 and -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요: 이 신발은 조금 ___ .
questions.explanation: For present inference, action verbs take -는 것 같다, adjectives take -(으)ㄴ 것 같다, and nouns take 인 것 같다.

grammar.meaning: than; comparison

questions.prompt: Compare size: 이 가방이 저 가방___ 더 커요.
questions.explanation: 보다 follows the item used as the comparison standard.

questions.prompt: Compare speed: 비행기가 기차___ 빨라요.
questions.explanation: 보다 follows the item used as the comparison standard.

grammar.meaning: a completed action modifying a noun

questions.prompt: Use 사다 for a completed purchase: 어제 ___ 책이 재미있어요.
questions.explanation: For a completed action modifying a noun, use -ㄴ after a vowel and -은 after most consonants: 산 책, 읽은 책.

questions.prompt: Use 읽다 for a completed action: 어제 ___ 책을 친구에게 줬어요.
questions.explanation: For a completed action modifying a noun, use -ㄴ after a vowel and -은 after most consonants: 산 책, 읽은 책.

grammar.meaning: choice or replacement

questions.prompt: Use N(으)로 for the replacement: 작은 가방___ 바꿔 주세요.
questions.explanation: N(으)로 can mark the item chosen or used as a replacement. Use 으로 after most consonants and 로 after a vowel or ㄹ.

questions.prompt: Use N(으)로 for the choice: 이 티셔츠___ 주세요.
questions.explanation: N(으)로 can mark the item chosen or used as a replacement. Use 으로 after most consonants and 로 after a vowel or ㄹ.

grammar.meaning: provide background or introduce a situation politely

questions.prompt: Use 찾다 with -는데요: 작은 가방을 ___ .
questions.explanation: Use -는데요 with action verbs, -(으)ㄴ데요 with adjectives, and 인데요 with nouns to introduce background or a situation.

questions.prompt: Use N인데요: 저는 새로 온 학생___ .
questions.explanation: Use -는데요 with action verbs, -(으)ㄴ데요 with adjectives, and 인데요 with nouns to introduce background or a situation.

grammar.meaning: predict or assume a future situation

questions.prompt: Predict using 춥다 and -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 내일은 날씨가 ___ .
questions.explanation: Besides plans, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 can express a prediction. 춥다 changes to 추울 거예요; 오다 becomes 올 거예요.

questions.prompt: Predict using 오다 and -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 하늘이 흐려요. 곧 비가 ___ .
questions.explanation: Besides plans, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 can express a prediction. 춥다 changes to 추울 거예요; 오다 becomes 올 거예요.

grammar.meaning: irregular 르 verbs and adjectives

questions.prompt: Use 다르다 in the polite present: 두 가방의 색이 ___ .
questions.explanation: For these 르-irregular stems, 으 drops and ㄹ is added to the previous syllable before -아/어요: 다르다 → 달라요, 모르다 → 몰라요.

questions.prompt: Use 모르다 in the polite present: 저는 그 주소를 ___ .
questions.explanation: For these 르-irregular stems, 으 drops and ㄹ is added to the previous syllable before -아/어요: 다르다 → 달라요, 모르다 → 몰라요.

grammar.meaning: it is enough to; all you need to do

questions.prompt: Use 누르다 with -(으)면 돼요: 이 버튼을 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)면 되다 describes a sufficient action. 르 does not change before the consonant ㅁ: 누르면 돼요. 쓰다 becomes 쓰면 돼요.

questions.prompt: Use 쓰다 with -(으)면 돼요: 여기에 이름을 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)면 되다 describes a sufficient action. 르 does not change before the consonant ㅁ: 누르면 돼요. 쓰다 becomes 쓰면 돼요.

vocab.en: to prepare for a lesson/study in advance

grammar.meaning: every; each

questions.prompt: Say every weekend: 주말___ 방을 청소해요.
questions.explanation: 마다 follows a noun and means every or each: 주말마다, 아침마다.

questions.prompt: Say every morning: 아침___ 산책해요.
questions.explanation: 마다 follows a noun and means every or each: 주말마다, 아침마다.

grammar.meaning: offer or promise an action

questions.prompt: Offer using 닦다 and -(으)ㄹ게요: 제가 바닥을 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses the speaker's offer or promise, often in response to the listener. Spell 게요, not 께요.

questions.prompt: Promise using 가다 and -(으)ㄹ게요: 제가 먼저 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses the speaker's offer or promise, often in response to the listener. Spell 게요, not 께요.

grammar.meaning: before doing an action

questions.prompt: Use 자다 and -기 전에: ___ 이를 닦아요.
questions.explanation: Attach -기 전에 to the verb stem for before doing something. Do not add the past marker to the first verb.

questions.prompt: Use 나가다 and -기 전에: 집에서 ___ 창문을 닫아요.
questions.explanation: Attach -기 전에 to the verb stem for before doing something. Do not add the past marker to the first verb.

grammar.meaning: after doing an action

questions.prompt: Use 먹다 and -(으)ㄴ 후에: 밥을 ___ 이를 닦아요.
questions.explanation: Use -은 후에 after most consonants and -ㄴ 후에 after a vowel for an action completed before the following action.

questions.prompt: Use 끝나다 and -(으)ㄴ 후에: 수업이 ___ 집에 갔어요.
questions.explanation: Use -은 후에 after most consonants and -ㄴ 후에 after a vowel for an action completed before the following action.

grammar.meaning: ask for a guess or prediction

questions.prompt: Ask for a prediction using 막히다: 지금 출발하면 길이 ___?
questions.explanation: Here -(으)ㄹ까요 asks for a prediction, rather than suggesting a joint action. 막히다 → 막힐까요, 춥다 → 추울까요.

questions.prompt: Ask for a prediction using 춥다 and -(으)ㄹ까요?: 내일 날씨가 ___?
questions.explanation: Here -(으)ㄹ까요 asks for a prediction, rather than suggesting a joint action. 막히다 → 막힐까요, 춥다 → 추울까요.

grammar.pattern: V/A-(으)ㄹ 것 같다, N일 것 같다
grammar.meaning: guess about a future event or likely identity

questions.prompt: Use 오다 with -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요: 구름이 많아요. 곧 비가 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 expresses a guess or prediction. With a noun, use 일 것 같다.

questions.prompt: Use N일 것 같아요 to guess an identity: 저 사람은 선생님___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 expresses a guess or prediction. With a noun, use 일 것 같다.

grammar.meaning: know or not know an embedded question

questions.prompt: Use 있다 with -는지: 은행이 어디에 ___ 알아요?
questions.explanation: Use -는지 with action verbs and 있다/없다, or 인지 with nouns, to embed a question before 알다 or 모르다.

questions.prompt: Use N인지: 이 사람이 누구___ 알아요?
questions.explanation: Use -는지 with action verbs and 있다/없다, or 인지 with nouns, to embed a question before 알다 or 모르다.

grammar.meaning: interrupt or switch an action

questions.prompt: Use 읽다 and -다가: 책을 ___ 잠이 들었어요.
questions.explanation: Attach -다가 to the verb stem when an ongoing action is interrupted or another event occurs during it.

questions.prompt: Use 가다 and -다가: 학교에 ___ 친구를 만났어요.
questions.explanation: Attach -다가 to the verb stem when an ongoing action is interrupted or another event occurs during it.

grammar.meaning: decide or agree to do something

questions.prompt: Use 만나다 and -기로 했어요: 내일 역에서 ___ .
questions.explanation: Attach -기로 하다 to the verb stem to describe a decision or agreement. The past form often reports a decision already made.

questions.prompt: Use 공부하다 and -기로 했어요: 방학에 한국어를 ___ .
questions.explanation: Attach -기로 하다 to the verb stem to describe a decision or agreement. The past form often reports a decision already made.

grammar.meaning: be thinking of doing something

questions.prompt: Use 가다 and -(으)ㄹ까 해요: 이번 주말에는 산에 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ까 하다 expresses a tentative plan: 갈까 해요, 먹을까 해요.

questions.prompt: Use 먹다 and -(으)ㄹ까 해요: 저녁에는 비빔밥을 ___ .
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ까 하다 expresses a tentative plan: 갈까 해요, 먹을까 해요.

grammar.meaning: a future or intended action modifying a noun

questions.prompt: Use 읽다 for an intended action: 내일 ___ 책을 골랐어요.
questions.explanation: Use -(으)ㄹ before a noun for a future or intended action: 읽을 책, 먹을 음식.

questions.prompt: Use 먹다 for an intended action: 내일 ___ 음식을 준비했어요.
questions.explanation: Use -(으)ㄹ before a noun for a future or intended action: 읽을 책, 먹을 음식.

grammar.meaning: intention or expectation as the basis for a request

questions.prompt: Use 만들다 with -(으)ㄹ 테니까: 제가 음식을 ___ 식탁을 준비해 주세요.
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 테니까 gives the speaker's intention or expectation as a basis for what follows. ㄹ-final 만들다 becomes 만들 테니까; 춥다 becomes 추울 테니까.

questions.prompt: Use 춥다 with -(으)ㄹ 테니까: 밤에는 ___ 따뜻한 옷을 가져가세요.
questions.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 테니까 gives the speaker's intention or expectation as a basis for what follows. ㄹ-final 만들다 becomes 만들 테니까; 춥다 becomes 추울 테니까.

grammar.meaning: look or appear to have a quality

questions.prompt: Use 피곤하다 and -아/어 보여요: 오늘 많이 ___ .
questions.explanation: Attach -아/어 보이다 to an adjective to describe how something appears: 피곤해 보여요, 맛있어 보여요.

questions.prompt: Use 맛있다 and -아/어 보여요: 이 음식이 정말 ___ .
questions.explanation: Attach -아/어 보이다 to an adjective to describe how something appears: 피곤해 보여요, 맛있어 보여요.

grammar.meaning: suggest an action; how about doing it?

questions.prompt: Suggest using 쉬다 and -는 게 어때요?: 오늘은 집에서 ___?
questions.explanation: Verb stem + 는 게 어때요 suggests an action. Here 게 is the contracted form of 것이.

questions.prompt: Suggest using 가다 and -는 게 어때요?: 주말에 공원에 ___?
questions.explanation: Verb stem + 는 게 어때요 suggests an action. Here 게 is the contracted form of 것이.

grammar.meaning: irregular ㅅ verbs

questions.prompt: Use 낫다 in the polite past: 감기가 다 ___ .
questions.explanation: In ㅅ-irregular verbs, ㅅ drops before a vowel ending: 낫다 → 나았어요, 짓다 → 지었어요. Not all ㅅ-final verbs are irregular.

questions.prompt: Use 짓다 in the polite past: 작년에 집을 ___ .
questions.explanation: In ㅅ-irregular verbs, ㅅ drops before a vowel ending: 낫다 → 나았어요, 짓다 → 지었어요. Not all ㅅ-final verbs are irregular.

grammar.meaning: infer a past action

questions.prompt: Infer with 먹다 and -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요: 접시가 비었어요. 동생이 과자를 다 ___ .
questions.explanation: For an inferred completed action, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같다: 먹은 것 같아요, 간 것 같아요. Keep this distinct from present and future inference.

questions.prompt: Infer with 가다 and -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요: 민수 씨가 안 보여요. 벌써 집에 ___ .
questions.explanation: For an inferred completed action, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같다: 먹은 것 같아요, 간 것 같아요. Keep this distinct from present and future inference.
